title: Telara evaluation: pilot security checklist + throughput scoping
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + ISO summary and network diagram (Jules) by 2025-11-24
SE to run 10K-token throughput micro-benchmark with Telara sample prompt set (Maya) by 2025-11-28
Schedule on-prem/private deployment architecture review with Telara infra (week of 2025-12-01)
Telara to share PII / PHI sample data redaction requirements and retention policy (Priya) by 2025-11-26
action_items: Jules - Send pricing tiers and pilot contract template - due 2025-11-24
Maya - Run latency/throughput test 8-GPU equivalent sim with Telara prompts - due 2025-11-28
Priya - Provide list of compliance controls required beyond SOC2 (encryption at rest KMS, HSM) - due 2025-11-26

summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on pilot success criteria (latency, cost per token, throughput), dataset/privacy constraints, and security/compliance gating (SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs). Agreed to run a small micro-benchmark and exchange security artifacts; next meeting to finalize pilot SLA and timeline.
topics: Security/compliance: SOC2 / ISO expectations, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging
Private deployment options (VPC, on-prem) and network requirements
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jules Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 55 minutes today. Quick intros?
[00:00:12] Evan Li: Evan from Telara, I lead the ML team. We're evaluating inference platforms for our patient-facing summarization workflows.
[00:00:20] Priya Singh: Priya, security. I'll be narrowing the compliance gate for the pilot — SOC2 but also some ISO asks.
[00:00:28] Maya Patel: Maya, SE at Redwood. I'll walk through the throughput and bench plan after we map out success criteria.
[00:00:34] Tom Alvarez: Tom, eng manager, I'll provide traffic patterns and infra constraints.
[00:00:40] Jules Carter: Great. High-level goal: Telara wants a 6-8 week pilot to prove latency & cost viability for a summarization feature that will be in our mobile app. Success criteria? Evan, do you want to say what success looks like from product?
[00:00:55] Evan Li: Yeah, so primary metric is p95 latency under 600ms for a 512-token response; throughput target is around 50 concurrent requests at peak, avg request payload ~1.2k tokens. Accuracy / QA — we have an eval rubric we'll share.
[00:01:11] Sara Gomes: We'll need < 2% hallucination regression compared to baseline model. Also retention and redaction — we can't send raw PHI outside our VPC without tokenization.
[00:01:23] Priya Singh: On compliance: SOC2 Type II is required for production. For pilot, acceptable to have SOC2 in progress plus SOC2 summary and controls mapping. We also need evidence of encryption at rest with KMS, SAML SSO integration, RBAC mapping to our roles, and immutable audit logs for all inference requests tied to user IDs.
[00:01:40] Jules Carter: Understood. For SOC2 we can share our SOC2 report and the controls matrix; for ISO we have a gap summary we can provide. For KMS we integrate with customer-managed KMS — is that a hard requirement?
[00:01:54] Priya Singh: For pilot we'd like to see KMS-backed key encryption, and an option to bring-your-own-key for private deployments. Also HSM for the long term if needed.
[00:02:03] Maya Patel: Noted. On the bench/throughput side, can you confirm the request size distribution and concurrency across regions? That will determine batching configs and whether we need Dedicated or can do Hosted with reserved capacity.
[00:02:15] Tom Alvarez: We're US-east heavy initially, ~70% traffic. Peak concurrency 50, p50 latency target 200ms, p95 600ms as Evan said. Payloads vary; sometimes compressed docs 2k tokens, average 1.2k.
[00:02:30] Maya Patel: Ok. For the micro-benchmark we'll simulate 10K synthetic requests across a 1-hour window with mixed sequence lengths to get cost-per-token and tail latency. We'll produce token breakdowns and suggest quantization levels.
[00:02:45] Evan Li: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching for repeated prompts? That affects cost a lot.
[00:02:52] Maya Patel: We support KV cache reuse for conversational flows and prefix caching for static context. In Dedicated we can pin longer caches; in Hosted we have configurable TTLs. We'll show numbers in the bench.
[00:03:03] Priya Singh: Audit logs: we need per-request logs with hashed user id (not PII), timestamp, model version, input token length, response token length, and a request-id that aligns with our internal tracing. Can you forward retention policies?
[00:03:17] Jules Carter: Yes, we can export audit logs to your S3 with encryption and configurable retention; we also stream to CloudWatch/GCP if preferred. Retention is configurable; for pilot we usually do 90 days.
[00:03:28] Priya Singh: 90 days is fine for pilot, but we'll document required retention for production separately. Also need proof of immutability / append-only logs for compliance.
[00:03:37] Maya Patel: We use signed append-only logs in the Dedicated/private control plane; we can show the audit trail export format.
[00:03:44] Tom Alvarez: On networking, we need a VPC peering pattern or private link. Also firewall rules — can Redwood support static egress IP ranges for whitelisting?
[00:03:54] Jules Carter: Yes, Dedicated supports static egress and VPC peering. Hosted has region-based egress ranges — we can provide the list for telara-east.
[00:04:04] Sara Gomes: About data residency: our app stores data in EU and US; initially pilot will be US-only but production might need EU hosting.
[00:04:12] Maya Patel: We can pin model routing by region; for EU you can select a datacenter region with the private deployment option.
[00:04:20] Evan Li: Bench specifics — we want both latency under load and regression tests vs our baseline model. Can you run an A/B micro-test?
[00:04:27] Maya Patel: Yes, we can run A/B against a pinned model version and collect accuracy metrics against your eval set. We'll need the eval prompts and expected outputs.
[00:04:36] Evan Li: We'll share 2k eval prompts with labels. Expect some tokenization differences, so guardrails for post-processing will be needed.
[00:04:44] Priya Singh: Also, SSO: we use SAML-based SSO with SCIM for user provisioning. We need test accounts to validate RBAC mapping to our teams.
[00:04:53] Jules Carter: We support SAML and SCIM; we'll exchange metadata and do a test-idp integration in staging. For RBAC we map roles to least privilege and can sync groups via SCIM.
[00:05:03] Tom Alvarez: For private deployments, what's deployment footprint? Our infra team prefers an air-gapped option but we may start with VPC-only private control plane.
[00:05:12] Maya Patel: Private control plane with customer-managed network requires a small control VM cluster plus inference nodes; we have an on-prem package for fully air-gapped but that adds lead time ~8-10 weeks. VPC/private control plane is faster ~2-3 weeks for pilot onboarding.
[00:05:26] Priya Singh: That lead time makes sense. For pilot we prefer VPC private control plane to meet data controls and still iterate quickly.
[00:05:33] Jules Carter: Timeline: propose 6-week pilot. Week 0-1: SSO + KMS + connectivity; week 2: bench runs and smoke tests; week 3-4: evaluation and model tuning; week 5-6: wrap-up and decision. Any blockers?
[00:05:47] Evan Li: Need security docs by Thurs and bench config by next Friday. Also a clear SLA matrix for Dedicated vs Hosted.
[00:05:55] Jules Carter: We'll send SOC2/ISO summary and the SLA matrix. Also will include pricing scenarios for Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted per-token.
[00:06:04] Sara Gomes: On legal: procurement asked about data processing addendum and standard contract redlines. Can you share the DPA?
[00:06:12] Jules Carter: Yes I'll attach the DPA and pilot terms; legal can handle standard redlines.
[00:06:17] Maya Patel: A few technical clarifications I'll note: 1) tokenization must be identical between eval scripts and bench harness, we'll provide tokenizer versions; 2) we recommend 8-bit quantization test for cost tradeoffs but will preserve quality checks; 3) KV cache TTLs will be adjustable per route.
[00:06:33] Tom Alvarez: For monitoring, we need token-level cost breakdown and per-model latency dashboards in Grafana. Can you pipeline metrics to our observability?
[00:06:41] Jules Carter: Yes, we can forward metrics via Prometheus remote write or direct CloudWatch metrics. We'll include dashboards.
[00:06:48] Priya Singh: Last question: audit of keys — do you provide audit for KMS operations and HSM usage?
[00:06:55] Maya Patel: For customer-managed KMS we don't have access to keys; we surface events around key usage and we can provide KMS audit logs forwarded to your logging bucket. For HSM-backed keys in private deployment we can produce attestation reports.
[00:07:07] Evan Li: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[00:07:11] Jules Carter: Recap: Redwood to share SOC2 summary, ISO gap report, DPA, network egress ranges, SLA matrix, pricing, and bench plan. Maya to run micro-bench and share results. Telara to send eval set and compliance gap list. We'll reconvene after bench results to finalize pilot kick-off.
[00:07:31] Sara Gomes: Thanks all.
[00:07:33] Jules Carter: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and calendar invites.
[00:07:38] [call end]
